transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called this case conference under our pre-filing practice so that employment, forensics, and insurance counsel can each report any material issues before I make the filing decision on our preliminary injunction. As you all know, we have a former sales executive who left last week for a direct competitor, we believe confidential customer information may have been used post-departure, and we have a hearing that could be requested within three weeks. Our draft filing currently seeks broad relief covering customer information, pricing materials, and source-code documentation. I'd like to go around the room — employment counsel, can you start by reporting any material issues on your end?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a material issue. While reviewing the former executive's archived personnel file, I found a signed separation agreement containing an exclusive forum clause. It requires that disputes about confidential information be filed in Illinois state court in Cook County, where the executive worked. I have not yet added this clause to the draft strategy memorandum. This could significantly affect where we file our preliminary injunction, so we need to consider it before any filing decision is signed.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to report a material issue from the forensics side. I reviewed the access logs and forensic image this week, and I can confirm that the only company data copied to the executive's device was the customer-list database. My review did not show any copying of pricing materials or source-code documentation. However, I have not yet updated the evidence chart to reflect these findings. This is directly relevant to our draft filing, which currently seeks broad relief covering all three categories — customer information, pricing materials, and source-code documentation. The forensic support for the pricing and source-code claims is not there based on what I've found so far.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a material insurance issue. I confirmed with our broker this week that our cyber-and-crime endorsement requires the carrier's written consent before we seek injunctive relief against an employee. This confirmation is still outside the litigation file, so it hasn't been reflected in our filing materials yet. If we proceed with the preliminary injunction without obtaining the carrier's written consent first, we could jeopardize coverage. This needs to be resolved before any filing decision is signed.
transcript.speaker: A4
